skill.name: metabolomics-workbench-database
skill.description: Query the NIH Metabolomics Workbench REST API for compounds, public studies, RefMet names, mass-spectrometry matches, and gene or protein records.
skill.summary: Build focused Metabolomics Workbench queries and interpret public metabolomics records.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: The skill documents expected read-only queries to the fixed NIH Metabolomics Workbench HTTPS API; no credential access, arbitrary destination, prompt injection, or covert exfiltration was found. Most alerts are safe API examples or Markdown syntax. One medium filesystem issue remains because download examples can overwrite structure.png without confirmation.

remediation.issue: Download examples can overwrite structure.png in the current directory.
remediation.suggestion: Require an explicit destination, check whether it exists, and ask before replacing an existing file.

content.value_statement: Finding consistent metabolite, study, and mass-spectrometry records across a large repository can require detailed API knowledge. This skill guides precise Metabolomics Workbench REST queries and structured interpretation.
actual_capabilities: Query compound records by PubChem, KEGG, HMDB, formula, registry number, and other documented identifiers.
Retrieve public study summaries, factors, measured metabolites, experimental data, and mwTab records.
Standardize metabolite names and inspect RefMet classifications.
Search candidate compounds by mass-to-charge ratio, adduct, database, and tolerance.
Filter studies by analytical method, polarity, chromatography, species, sample source, disease, or metabolite.
Look up documented gene and protein records linked to metabolism.
limitations: The skill requires network access to the public Metabolomics Workbench service.
API availability, record completeness, and response formats remain controlled by the external service.
The examples do not add retries, timeouts, rate controls, or comprehensive response validation.
Mass matches are candidates and require experimental confirmation before biological interpretation.

use_cases.title: Find Relevant Public Studies
use_cases.description: Search studies by standardized metabolite, disease, sample source, or analytical platform, then summarize matching records.

use_cases.title: Triage Mass-Spectrometry Features
use_cases.description: Generate candidate compounds for an observed mass, adduct, and tolerance, then compare identifiers and classifications.

use_cases.title: Build Reproducible Data Retrieval
use_cases.description: Select documented endpoints and output fields for a repeatable public-data collection workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Look Up a Study
prompt_templates.prompt: Find the public Metabolomics Workbench summary for study {study_id}. Report the title, species, sample source, disease, platform, and measured metabolites.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner lookup using a known study identifier

prompt_templates.title: Standardize a Metabolite
prompt_templates.prompt: Standardize {metabolite_name} with RefMet. Return the preferred name, formula, exact mass, identifiers, and structural classification when available.

prompt_templates.title: Search an Observed Mass
prompt_templates.prompt: Search {database} for m/z {mass} using adduct {adduct} and tolerance {tolerance}. Rank plausible candidates and explain which fields require validation.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Study Comparison
prompt_templates.prompt: Find public {species} {sample_source} studies about {disease} using {platform}. Standardize reported metabolites and create a comparison of study design, methods, and coverage.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow combining study filters, RefMet, and experimental metadata

output_examples.input: Standardize citrate and identify its RefMet classification.
output_examples.output: Preferred name: Citrate. The result includes formula, exact mass, available identifiers, and its RefMet hierarchy, with missing fields clearly marked.

output_examples.input: Find human blood diabetes studies using LC-MS HILIC in positive mode.
output_examples.output: A study comparison lists matching identifiers, titles, investigators, sample details, analytical methods, and links to available public records.

output_examples.input: Search m/z 180.0634 with M+H and a 0.01 Da tolerance.
output_examples.output: Candidate metabolites are ordered by mass agreement and include registry identifiers, formulas, exact masses, names, and a reminder that standards must confirm identity.

best_practices: Standardize metabolite names with RefMet before searching studies.
Choose the adduct and mass tolerance from the actual acquisition method.
Validate identifiers, HTTP status, response shape, and missing fields before analysis.
anti_patterns: Do not treat an m/z match as a confirmed compound identification.
Do not send private sample data or unpublished subject information in public API paths.
Do not overwrite downloaded files or issue large request batches without explicit controls.

faq.question: Does this skill require an API key?
faq.answer: The documented public REST endpoints do not use an API key.

faq.question: Which data formats are supported?
faq.answer: The API documentation covers JSON and tab-delimited text. Some compound endpoints also return molecular structure files or PNG images.

faq.question: Can it standardize metabolite names?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses RefMet matching and classification endpoints to find preferred names and related chemical fields.

faq.question: Can it identify a compound from m/z alone?
faq.answer: It can return candidates for a mass, adduct, and tolerance. Experimental evidence and reference standards are still required for confirmation.

faq.question: Can it retrieve complete study data?
faq.answer: It can request public study data and mwTab records when the repository exposes them.

faq.question: Does it modify local files?
faq.answer: Most queries only read remote data. Structure download examples can write structure.png, so confirm the destination before running them.
